To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the physical-chemical properties of DNA can be used as a powerful tool for the annotation of the P. faloiparum genome.
the coding regions of the P. falariparum genes are regions of high thermal DNA stability.
(1) the P. faloiparum genome has a high AT content, (2) the coding sequences have a high thermal stability, and (3) the coding sequences can be identified as regions of thermal stability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the problem of gene identification.
the development of a new approach for the annotation of the P. falariparum genome.
the development and the application of a physical criterion for gene identification, and with the annotation of a genome of particular interest for medical research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the physical criterion provides a powerful and convenient approach to the annotation of the P. falariparum genome.
the structural analysis provides a very valuable tool for gene identification, but that the results must be interpreted and used with caution.
the physical criterion of thermal stability of the DNA helix is a valid and convenient tool for identifying the coding regions in the P. falciparum genome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the P. falarum genome is not as complex as previously thought.
the structural analyses of the P. faloiparum genome have led to a new, and more complete, annotation of the genome.

, for the P. faloiparum genome, the physical criterion is a powerful tool for the identification, or the revision, of the coding regions, and that the structural analyses provide a convenient alternative to the database annotations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gene annotation of P. falciparium is far from complete, and that new approaches to the gene identification problem are needed.
, in the case of the P. faloiparium genome, the physical - thermal stability of the double-helical DNA is a reliable and efficient criterion for the identification of the coding sequences.
the structural analysis of genomic sequences can provide an important contribution to the annotation problem.
